role: calibration only (four-term ES as triviality control)
missing_theorem: None: 4-term solutions are plentiful, and the merge 4 → 3 is ES (Q03 recurring theorem 1).

role: polynomial-method (Combinatorial Nullstellensatz) certificate of existence
missing_theorem: A polynomial P_p over a finite field whose non-vanishing coefficient forces an ES witness. Such arguments produce solutions over F_q, and ES is locally trivial; lifting to positive integers is the integral problem. A mod-ℓ count argument also holds at odd squares (T1).
status_ref: FRONTIER §1 (no local obstruction), T1; M-pattern row M5
note: The prime-sized-seat theorem is about F_p structure; ES's difficulty is archimedean plus integral.

role: calibration only (omitted values with a sharp primality criterion)
missing_theorem: None for ES: slice failures are confinement events (e.g. C = 1: 4p + 1 has no prime factor ≡ 3 mod 4), not primality, except in siblings with a vacuous level-1 class (Z1982: 2n + 5 prime).

role: calibration only (residue compression of exceptional sets)
missing_theorem: None new: (★)-zeros ≤ 10¹⁰ are all ≡ 1 (mod 8) (BM: χ_p(2) sign), and class means mod 840 follow RESIDUE_HARDNESS.

role: stratify by square factors of the tied integers and handle all but a squarefree residual
missing_theorem: ES holds whenever some 4Cp + 1 (C ≤ K) has a square factor of suitable shape; then treat the squarefree residual. No yield: square factors do not produce divisors ≡ −1 (mod 4C) (ℓ² ≡ 1 when ℓ ≡ ±1), and the squarefree residual has positive density (∏(1 − 2/ℓ²)-type), so it is the generic case.
status_ref: elementary; Borwein–Choi template (A025052) does not transfer to residue conditions
note: The thin stratum is not where ES's difficulty is.

role: calibration only (boundary/degenerate parameter cases)
missing_theorem: None: degenerate cases (zero, negative or repeated denominators) are the signed/boundary terms β_t of METAPLECTIC_ES (K2), handled exactly.

role: calibration only (Collatz: almost-all is not pointwise)
missing_theorem: None for ES.

role: calibration only (lonely runner torus avoidance)
missing_theorem: None for ES.

role: calibration only (lonely runner symmetry reduction)

role: cover-then-absorb (EFL/absorption method): cheap certificates for most p plus a reserved absorber for the rest
missing_theorem: There is a family A of certificates set aside in advance such that every prime missed by the cheap families is certified by some member of A. In combinatorics absorbers work because one may choose objects with power-size multiplicity (M4). In ES, p is forced and the residual primes are exactly those where every tied event fails. An absorber would be a certificate family guaranteed to hit the residual, i.e. ES on the residual.
status_ref: FRONTIER §3 M-pattern row M4 ('p and K = (p+q)/4 are forced'); B2
note: Absorption needs freedom to choose the objects, which ES lacks.

role: calibration only (EFL hypergraph vs arithmetic family)
missing_theorem: Same as Z2251.

role: T1 model: reciprocity-obstructed families in Apollonian packings (quadratic and quartic)
missing_theorem: A higher-reciprocity (e.g. quartic) obstruction for ES at a thin family of primes, as in HKRS. Closed: TWO_POWER_LADDER Thm 3.2 (m = 4) shows the Stickelberger component determines the ES datum only up to a free sign, so quartic reciprocity forces nothing; for m = 3 it says nothing. No odd-order BM layer exists. A 'prime T1' stays open in principle (FRONTIER §7.15).
note: The Apollonian quartic family has no ES analogue at m = 4 because D² = S².

role: calibration only (Ringel packing: complementary coverings)
missing_theorem: None: complementary certificate lines are finite menus (B1/B2(iii)). The smallest uncovered classes are Z1953's quantity.

role: calibration only (EFL: colourings as congruence coverings)
missing_theorem: None: congruence coverings of the hard classes are excluded (B1).

role: calibration only (word problem: equality vs existence)
missing_theorem: None: SL₂(ℤ) normal forms are standard; ES asks for existence of a word with a tied congruence.

role: calibration only (addition-chain recurrences / certificate extension n ↦ 2n + c)
missing_theorem: None: the only certificate extension is multiplicative (ES(d) ⇒ ES(kd)). Additive recurrences n ↦ an + c give polynomial families, which are B1 at primes ((J)84).

role: calibration only (universal Diophantine statements with multiplicative closure)
missing_theorem: None. Correction to Pass 1: ES does have multiplicative closure (a solution for d | n scales to n), which is exactly how it reduces to primes p ≡ 1 (4).

role: calibration only (local solubility without integral points)
missing_theorem: None: ES has local solubility everywhere and no BM obstruction; a counterexample would be non-BM (the Markoff precedent).

role: identity families with factored obstruction polynomials; intersect their failure sets
missing_theorem: Finitely many parametrised identity families whose failure sets have empty intersection at primes. False: finite unions of polynomial/identity families miss the square classes (Mordell–Schinzel), and under H every finite menu fails i.o.

role: Lagrange-type descent: from ES-type data at mp produce data at m′p with m′ < m
missing_theorem: A composition/descent law on structured solutions of 4/(mp) (e.g. m dividing two denominators) that strictly lowers m. Lagrange uses Euler's four-square composition (a norm form of a quaternion algebra, i.e. a group law). The ES surface is not homogeneous and has a finite automorphism group (S₃), so no composition law is visible. Matrix multiplication in the SL₂ form does not preserve the p-entry.
status_ref: FRONTIER §3 M-pattern row M3 (U_n not homogeneous, finite automorphism group); Z2358
barrier: M3; B2 (the final step of any descent is a tied divisor event)

role: calibration only (two-term conic 4/n = 1/x + 1/y)
missing_theorem: None new: a single divisor condition (Stewart; 4/p two-term ⟺ p ≡ 3 mod 4). The third variable converts it into a union over levels, the tied lottery (Q18 Z0408).

role: calibration only (weighted 4/p = 1/x + 1/y + 2/z is trivial)
missing_theorem: None. Verified identity: x = y = z = p, and for p ≡ 1 (4), x = (p + 3)/4 leaves 3/N with N = p(p + 3)/4 = 1/N + 2/N. Unit numerators are load-bearing.

role: calibration only (phase diagram of unions of single lines)
missing_theorem: None for ES. Each fixed level fails i.o. (CONDITIONAL on Dickson); (★) fails at 14 primes ≤ 10¹⁰; ES never fails ≤ 10¹⁸. The zero law P(f = 0) ≈ exp(−0.535 μ^{0.91}) is the measured phase diagram.

role: calibration only (symmetry group of the ES surface)
missing_theorem: None: in reciprocal coordinates the problem is the plane X + Y + Z = 4/n with all coordinates unit fractions. The automorphisms preserving positivity and integrality for infinitely many n are S₃ (finite), with no Vieta group; this is row M3 of the M-pattern.
status_ref: FRONTIER §3 M-pattern row M3; (J)89 (no Vieta involution)

role: calibration only (Mordell classes = square classes; identities cannot cover squares)
missing_theorem: None new: polynomial identities cover exactly the non-square classes mod M (Mordell–Schinzel; reciprocity). This holds for every M = 840·ℓ by the same argument.

role: calibration only (ladder m/n in m − 1 terms: 3/p two terms fails for p ≡ 1 mod 3)
missing_theorem: None new: 3/p = 1/x + 1/y ⟺ p has a divisor pair with sum ≡ 0 (mod 3), so for prime p it fails iff p ≡ 1 (3) (Stewart); 4/p two-term ⟺ p ≡ 3 (4).

role: calibration only (GRH successes: bounded L-function families)
missing_theorem: None new: the GRH successes (least QNR, Artin density, Ramanujan's form) are fixed-modulus M2 events or averages; ES needs ≍ p characters χ_{−4uB} at once, and R(p) has no L-function (finite Dirichlet polynomial).
status_ref: FRONTIER §3 M-pattern row M2; out_Q18 Z0572

role: calibration only (two-sided exact formulas: r₄(n) = 8σ*(n))
missing_theorem: None: two-sided polylog asymptotics for R are false infinitely often (Linnik large values, BM_CORRECTED Prop 3.1); the exact theta-quotient form is Eisenstein-only.

role: continuity across the cone boundary: signed solutions with a small negative denominator
missing_theorem: Counts of signed solutions (one negative denominator, |z| ≤ p^θ) decay to positive solutions as θ → 0 by a continuity/sign-change argument. False as a transfer: signed Type I slices have (|d|/p) = +1 and positive ones (d/p) = −1, so no |d|-preserving move links them, and class-changing transfers are B2.

role: Pratt-style recursion
missing_theorem: Same as Z2065 (known-false; factors of 4p + 1 at (★)-zeros are all ≡ 1 mod 4 and carry no class information).

This would make those barriers unconditional; it would not prove ES, since no ES proof uses Bateman–Horn as input. BST holds with probability 1 over height-ordered families, not for fixed polynomials.
status_ref: arXiv:2212.10373 (BST); FRONTIER §3 B1/B2; out_P00 Z2579 (same role over F_q[T] via Bary-Soroker)

note: Same verdict as P00 Z2579: it validates barriers.

role: calibration only (ILP for minimal sterile residue systems)
missing_theorem: None new: B1 depth is already quantified (POINTWISE_OMEGA13 Thm 5.1; STERILE_* files). An ILP would give constants only. Pass 1 estimated > 1 h to derive the constraints.

role: calibration only (positive density of large prime gaps vs long sterile slice runs)
missing_theorem: None: for fixed K the joint failure of slices C ≤ K has density ≍ (log p)^{−K/2}-type (Z1927 heuristic), not positive density. The analogue therefore fails, and no ES statement is calibrated by it.

role: calibration only (cubic characters and ES counts)
missing_theorem: None: TWO_POWER_LADDER (m = 3: the Stickelberger component says nothing about D). Pass 1: cubic character of 2 or 4 shows no correlation with R/log²p (Spearman −0.01).

role: calibration only (Ostmann inverse Goldbach)
missing_theorem: None: ES-good sets are closed under multiples (multiplicative), so additive decompositions are irrelevant.

role: local limit theorem for subset products of prime factors of 4Cp + 1 in (ℤ/4C)^×
missing_theorem: For every p some C has the sub-multiset products of the prime factors of N_C equidistributed enough to hit −1. Per level this fails: ω(N_C) ≍ log log p steps is far below the mixing time ≍ log φ(4C) for growing C, and fixed C is a finite menu. So it collapses to the union over levels, the lottery.
status_ref: out_Q18 Z0498 (sub-products = divisor condition); Juškevičius–Šemetulskis (anti-concentration, wrong direction)
note: LO gives upper bounds; the needed lower bound per level is false for most levels.

role: explicit sieve lower bounds via local models (Ramaré, Ramaré–Walker)
missing_theorem: A Ramaré-type explicit lower bound for the one-integer event at each p. Ramaré–Walker prove pointwise-in-the-modulus results (every class mod q contains a product of three primes ≤ q^{O(1)}) because the search box has power size (M1a). ES's event concerns the divisors of one integer, with a polylog expected count.
status_ref: FRONTIER §3 M-pattern row M1a; Ramaré–Walker arXiv:1610.05804
note: A 'thin-count precedent' it is not: its count is a power.

role: calibration only (extreme-value 'last hard prime' model)
missing_theorem: None for ES: Pass 1 fits κ ≈ 0.3 on (★)-zeros. The repo's zero law across numerators is the calibrated version, and model risk dominates P(ES false).

role: calibration only (prehomogeneous spaces: averages easy, pointwise hard)
missing_theorem: None.

role: ES₅ as 'Thue ratio set + divisibility': some QNR A ≡ u/v (u, v > 0) with uv | p + u + v
missing_theorem: For every prime p ≡ 1 (24) there are positive u, v with (u/p) ≠ (v/p) and uv | p + u + v. This is the bichromatic edge of the forest F_p (FRONTIER §7.2), i.e. ES₅. Thue's lemma covers every residue with signed small u, v; the divisibility is the entire content, and its heuristic count Σ 1/(uv) ≍ log²p is the M_BM scale.
status_ref: FRONTIER §3 'Rooted constructions' (forest F_n, certificate ⟺ bichromatic edge), §7.2; LOWER_TAIL_ASTRA (J)106

role: Deuring–Heilbronn-type dichotomy: sub-route failures explained by one extreme character
missing_theorem: Main-term layer, already true: the BM deficit is governed by a single character. T(p) = Σ(−uB/p)/φ(4uB) = (σ/4)E·L(1, χ_p)² + O(p^{−1/16} log p), and the (★)-zeros all have p ≡ 1 (8) with elevated L(1, χ_p) ∈ [2.3, 5.2] and M_BM/L² ∈ [0.083, 0.136] (typical ≈ 0.15). Open part: a dichotomy for the error R − M_BM ('if R(p) is small then χ_p is exceptional, and that case can be handled'). No mechanism exists, since the depressed main term is still ≫ log²p.
barrier: B3 (main term explains 4–5 % of the variance); B2 for the error
next: None new; BM_LVALUE §1.4 already ran the item's first step on all 14 (★)-zeros (and the b = 1 failures could be added to that table cheaply).

role: calibration only (powers-of-two slice x = 2^k)
missing_theorem: None: 37/8977 primes ≤ 2·10⁵ (0.41 %) have such a solution (Pass 1), so the slice is not a reservoir (cf. Q18 Z0870).
note: Linnik's 2^v works additively; ES's slice is multiplicative and thin.

role: Cauchy-lemma analogue: an inequality region in (s, q) = (u + B, uB) where a hit is forced
missing_theorem: A region 𝓡(p) in the (s, q) plane such that some (s, q) ∈ 𝓡(p) with s ≡ −p (mod 4q) and s² − 4q a square must exist. Cauchy's lemma rests on Gauss's three-squares theorem, a local-global principle for a one-class genus (M1a/M3) that is true at odd squares. ES's analogue must fail at squares (T1), and the class condition mod 4q is a height-dependent target (M1b).
note: The polygonal-number mechanism is genus-theoretic, hence T1-blind.

role: incidence lower bound (Furstenberg/Kakeya analogue) forcing a certificate in the (C, prime) incidence structure
missing_theorem: At fixed p, the incidences between residue lines {C ≡ −(4p)^{−1} (mod q)} and the divisibility conditions force some C with a divisor of 4Cp + 1 ≡ −1 (mod 4C). Lines for q larger than the level range meet at most one C (privacy of large primes), so the incidence structure among them is trivial. The non-trivial incidences involve only small q, i.e. congruence (B1) data.
status_ref: SYNTHESIS_SPARKS8 Lemma 2.3 (privacy of large primes); FRONTIER §4 line 10
note: Kakeya-type lower bounds need many overlapping tubes; ES's large primes are private to one level.

role: calibration only (power main terms are necessary but not sufficient)
missing_theorem: None for ES. It refines B3 Remark 2.4: a lift with a power main term must also have enough free variables for minor-arc control (binary problems such as p + m² stay open with a √n main term).
next: Close; add the 'dimension' caveat next to B3 Remark 2.4 if a lift is ever proposed (Z2060).

role: calibration only (b = 1 line as a 'Goldbach's other conjecture' model)
missing_theorem: None for ES. The b = 1 line fails at 193, 2521, 66529 ≤ 10¹¹. Testing that they sit at the low end of the b = 1 main term is a model calibration (EVIDENCE) of the zero law.

role: positivity trick (3-4-1) forcing non-vanishing of the finite level polynomial F_p(s) = Σ_C D_C(p)C^{−s}
missing_theorem: A non-negative trigonometric combination of twisted level counts Σ_k a_k F_p(χ^k) ≥ c·(untwisted mass) − error. Mertens' trick uses the Euler product of ζ (multiplicativity, log-positivity); F_p is a finite count with no Euler product. Any character-twist positivity reproduces the orthogonality detector 1[d ≡ −1 (mod 4C)], whose lower bound is the lower tail itself.
note: 3-4-1 needs an Euler product; R(p) is a count at one integer.

role: current-graph-style compact templates covering one Mordell-hard class mod a large modulus
missing_theorem: For a class r mod M, a finite list of parametric templates (depending on p mod M′) certifies every prime in the class. False for any finite list (B1 Thm C, CONDITIONAL on H). Measuring the growth of the greedy template count vs X is a calibration of B1 only.
status_ref: POINTWISE_SIZE Thm C; B2 Thm 2.2(iii); Z1953 (this batch)

role: Landau–Siegel 'at most one exceptional character' among the χ_{−4uB} in M_BM
missing_theorem: Already true in the strongest form: χ_{−4uB}(p) = (−uB/p) for every pair, so the whole BM deficit T(p) is a sum of values of the single character χ_p, and T(p) = (σ/4)E·L(1, χ_p)² + O(p^{−1/16} log p). Stephens' bound gives M_BM ≥ 0.92 M₀ at p ≡ 1 (8). Gap: the error term R − M_BM, which this does not touch.
note: There is literally one character, so the 'at most one exception' structure is automatic at the main-term level.

role: stickiness dichotomy: certificate-bearing levels sharing prime factors across levels
missing_theorem: Split configurations at fixed p into 'sticky' (levels C, C + kq sharing a prime q) and 'non-sticky', and force a certificate in each case. Levels share q only when q ≤ the level range (privacy of large primes), so stickiness is congruence data (B1). The certifying large prime factors are private, so the non-sticky half is the whole lottery.
status_ref: SYNTHESIS_SPARKS8 Lemma 2.3; FRONTIER §3 privacy of large primes
